message.reasoning:
I am ready to make a decision in this Monopoly turn.

I have $760 and three unmortgaged properties. p1 has an orange monopoly with $190 cash. p2 has a brown monopoly with $619 cash.

p4 is in jail with $366 cash and a get-out-of-jail-free card. p2 owns yellows, Reading Railroad, and almost a full yellow monopoly. The bank holds Virginia Avenue, Illinois Avenue, B&O Railroad, and North Carolina Avenue.

Boardwalk must stay unmortgaged. I will not feed p1 or give p2 Illinois. I will not give p4 North Carolina. I need $760 cash to survive orange hits. I should pass GO before hitting p1 again. I can mortgage Electric Company and Boardwalk for $275. I am weighing whether to trade.

I have no monopoly. Boardwalk is weak without Park Place. p2 still needs Illinois to complete the reds. p1's orange houses are heavily built.

p1 cannot afford to build the fourth house on St. James or Tennessee. Their $190 cash is too low for that $200 investment. I am calculating exact orange rent values to assess the real threat.

Orange rent values are now clear. p1 can charge $550 to $800 per hit. Boardwalk mortgage yields $200, Electric Company $75, and Kentucky $110. Combined with cash, this gives a $385 safety net against an $800 New York Avenue hit. Mortgaging everything would create $1145 total. Boardwalk should only be mortgaged if debt forces it.

I am now considering specific trades. Acquiring Park Place from p4 would complete a dark blue monopoly, but it costs $350 and requires $400 in house money, which would drain my cash against the orange threat. I am also weighing a trade with p2 for Kentucky.

I rejected giving Kentucky to p2 because that would leave them two-thirds of the red monopoly and dangerous if Illinois is rolled. Boardwalk must stay unmortgaged since it is the only path to a dark blue monopoly. I am now evaluating whether p4 will trade Park Place, though they may want to keep it as a blocker or for their own green monopoly.

I am now drafting a concrete trade proposal. I would offer cash plus Electric Company in exchange for Park Place. p4 is in jail with $366 and could use the cash to buy North Carolina when it lands. Building dark blue houses costs $200 each, so the rent payoff is steep.

I will end the turn and preserve cash. Acquiring Park Place now would leave me with too little money to build houses or survive p1's orange hits. I cannot buy unowned properties until I land on them.

I am now considering trading Kentucky to p4 for Park Place. This would complete my dark blue monopoly without spending cash. However, p4 might trade Kentucky back to p2 for Ventnor or North Carolina. That would give p2 two-thirds of the reds and a yellow monopoly.

A cash-plus-Kentucky offer for Park Place would still leave me with only about $610. That is too little to build even one house on each dark blue property and survive p1's orange rent hits. The immediate rent boost from the monopoly is not worth the risk. I will wait before building.

I will wait and collect the $200 GO bonus before buying Park Place. p4 is in jail and may be pressured to sell it. Trading with p1 or p2 is not viable.

Baltic and Mediterranean four-house rent totals $480, which is less threatening than p1's orange hits. p2 spent $400 building browns and now has $619 cash. I am considering buying Ventnor from p4 to permanently block p2's yellow monopoly, though it costs cash and does not complete my own set.

I am now weighing whether to buy Ventnor from p4. Blocking p2's yellow monopoly is critical, but spending $250 would leave me with only $510 against an $800 New York Avenue hit. p4 may not sell it cheaply, and p2 could outbid me for it. Without Ventnor, p2 might become the second major threat.

I will not buy Ventnor. I previously judged that overpaying for it would signal interest and risk p2 and p4 forming a yellow monopoly deal.

I will end the turn without revealing my strategy. I will not mortgage any properties. I am checking whether the engine will prompt again if I propose a trade.

I can propose a trade and still end the turn later. I will only offer a deal if it is clearly good. The best option is Park Place for a price I can afford while keeping enough cash to survive an $800 New York Avenue hit. My survival floor is roughly $945 without mortgaging Boardwalk.

Mortgaging Boardwalk after acquiring Park Place would destroy the dark blue monopoly. A mortgaged property cannot receive houses, and any mortgaged property in a set loses doubled rent. This makes the trade even less attractive.
